## Comparison to Age-Band subdivisions
```{r}
sex_age_subdivision_ma <- function(urine_component, data = urine_ma2) {

  # --- 1. Identify the correct columns -------------------------------
  mean_colname <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "volume_mean_m_l",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "ph_mean",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "creatinine_mean_mmol_24h",
    TRUE ~ paste0(urine_component, "_mean_mmol_24h")
  )
  
  sd_colname <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "volume_sd_m_l",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "ph_sd",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "creatinine_sd_mmol_24h",
    TRUE ~ paste0(urine_component, "_sd_mmol_24h")
  )
  
  urine_component_for_title <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "Volume (L/24h)",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "pH",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "Creatinine (mmol/24h)",
    TRUE ~ paste0(str_to_title(urine_component), " (mmol/24h)")
  )
  
  # --- 2. Prepare data with overall_bias for meta-regression --------
  data_with_bias <- data %>%
    left_join(overall_bias, by = "study_name")

  # --- 3. Get main meta-analysis result ----------------------------
  # Overall main result (all sexes, all ages)
  main_overall <- main_ma(urine_component, data = data) %>%
    mutate(sex_group = "main meta-analysis",
           age_band = "Overall")
  
  # Main meta-analysis by age band (all sexes combined)
  data_main <- data %>%
    select(
      study_name,
      total_n,
      age_band,
      mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
      sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
      study_type
    ) %>%
    drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
  
  age_bands_main <- data_main %>% 
    filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>% 
    pull(age_band) %>% 
    unique() %>% 
    sort()
  
  main_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_main, function(age) {
    data_age <- data_main %>% 
      filter(age_band == age)
    
    if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    
    run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, "main meta-analysis", age)
  })
  
  # Add meta-regression for main analysis
  main_meta_reg_results <- tryCatch({
    meta_regression("none", urine_component = urine_component)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Meta-regression failed for main analysis: ", e$message)
    NULL
  })
  
  main_result <- bind_rows(main_overall, main_age_results, main_meta_reg_results)
  
  # Sort Study type column
  data_main$study_type <- as.factor(data_main$study_type)
  study_type_main <- if (dplyr::n_distinct(data_main$study_type, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) {
    "Mixed"
  } else {
    unique(na.omit(data_main$study_type))
  }
  
  # --- 3b. RCT-only main analysis ----------------------------
  data_main_rct <- data %>%
    filter(study_type == "RCT") %>%
    select(
      study_name,
      total_n,
      age_band,
      study_type,
      mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
      sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname)
    ) %>%
    drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
  
  if (nrow(data_main_rct) > 0) {
    # Overall RCT result
    main_rct_overall <- run_single_ma(data_main_rct, urine_component, "main meta-analysis", "Overall (RCT only)")
    
    # RCT by age band
    main_rct_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_main, function(age) {
      data_age <- data_main_rct %>% 
        filter(age_band == age)
      
      if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }
      
      run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, "main meta-analysis", paste0(age, " (RCT only)"))
    })
    
    main_rct_result <- bind_rows(main_rct_overall, main_rct_age_results)
  } else {
    main_rct_result <- tibble()
  }
  
  # --- 4. Iterate through sexes and age bands --------------------------------
  sex_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(c("male", "female"), function(sex) {
    
    # First get overall result for this sex (all age bands)
    data_sex <- data %>% 
      filter(male_female == sex) %>%
      select(
        study_name,
        total_n,
        age_band,
        mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
        sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
        study_type
      ) %>%
      drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
    
    if (nrow(data_sex) == 0) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    
    # Get overall result for this sex
    overall_result <- run_single_ma(data_sex, urine_component, sex, "Overall")
    
    # Sort Study type column
    data_sex$study_type <- as.factor(data_sex$study_type)
    study_type_sex <- if (dplyr::n_distinct(data_sex$study_type, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) {
      "Mixed"
    } else {
      unique(na.omit(data_sex$study_type))
    }
    
    # Get meta-regression result for this sex
    meta_reg_result <- tryCatch({
      meta_regression(data_subset = sex, urine_component = urine_component)
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("Meta-regression failed for ", sex, ": ", e$message)
      NULL
    })
    
    # Get unique age bands
    age_bands <- data_sex %>% 
      filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>% 
      pull(age_band) %>% 
      unique() %>% 
      sort()
    
    # Get results for each age band
    age_band_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands, function(age) {
      data_age <- data_sex %>% 
        filter(age_band == age)
      
      if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }
      
      run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, sex, age)
    })
    
    # --- RCT-only analyses for this sex ---
    data_sex_rct <- data_sex %>%
      filter(study_type == "RCT")
    
    if (nrow(data_sex_rct) > 0) {
      # Overall RCT for this sex
      rct_overall <- run_single_ma(data_sex_rct, urine_component, sex, "Overall (RCT only)")
      
      # RCT by age band for this sex
      rct_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands, function(age) {
        data_age <- data_sex_rct %>% 
          filter(age_band == age)
        
        if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
          return(tibble())
        }
        
        run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, sex, paste0(age, " (RCT only)"))
      })
      
      rct_sex_results <- bind_rows(rct_overall, rct_age_results)
    } else {
      rct_sex_results <- tibble()
    }
    
    # Combine overall, age band, meta-regression, and RCT results
    bind_rows(overall_result, age_band_results, meta_reg_result, rct_sex_results)
  })
  
  # --- 4b. Quality sensitivity analyses (Low bias only; Low + Moderate bias) ----
  # Join data with bias ratings for quality filtering
  data_with_quality <- data_with_bias

  quality_filters <- list(
    "Low Risk of Bias Only" = c("Low"),
    "Low + Moderate Risk of Bias" = c("Low", "Moderate")
  )

  quality_results <- purrr::map_dfr(names(quality_filters), function(filter_name) {
    filter_levels <- quality_filters[[filter_name]]
    data_quality <- data_with_quality %>%
      filter(overall %in% filter_levels)

    if (nrow(data_quality) == 0) {
      message("No studies match quality filter '", filter_name, "' for ", urine_component)
      return(tibble())
    }

    # Prepare quality-filtered data
    data_q_main <- data_quality %>%
      select(
        study_name, total_n, age_band,
        mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
        sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
        study_type
      ) %>%
      drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)

    if (nrow(data_q_main) == 0) return(tibble())

    # --- Main MA (overall) ---
    q_main_overall <- tryCatch({
      main_ma(urine_component, data = data_quality) %>%
        mutate(sex_group = "main meta-analysis", age_band = "Overall")
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("Quality MA failed (main overall, ", filter_name, "): ", e$message)
      tibble()
    })

    # --- Main MA by age band ---
    q_age_bands <- data_q_main %>%
      filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>%
      pull(age_band) %>%
      unique() %>%
      sort()

    q_main_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(q_age_bands, function(age) {
      data_age <- data_q_main %>% filter(age_band == age)
      if (nrow(data_age) == 0) return(tibble())
      tryCatch(
        run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, "main meta-analysis", age),
        error = function(e) tibble()
      )
    })

    # --- Sex subdivision ---
    q_sex_results <- purrr::map_dfr(c("male", "female"), function(sex) {
      data_sex <- data_quality %>%
        filter(male_female == sex) %>%
        select(
          study_name, total_n, age_band,
          mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
          sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
          study_type
        ) %>%
        drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)

      if (nrow(data_sex) == 0) return(tibble())

      # Overall for this sex
      sex_overall <- tryCatch(
        run_single_ma(data_sex, urine_component, sex, "Overall"),
        error = function(e) tibble()
      )

      # By age band for this sex
      age_bands_sex <- data_sex %>%
        filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>%
        pull(age_band) %>%
        unique() %>%
        sort()

      sex_age_results_q <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_sex, function(age) {
        data_age <- data_sex %>% filter(age_band == age)
        if (nrow(data_age) == 0) return(tibble())
        tryCatch(
          run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, sex, age),
          error = function(e) tibble()
        )
      })

      bind_rows(sex_overall, sex_age_results_q)
    })

    bind_rows(q_main_overall, q_main_age_results, q_sex_results) %>%
      mutate(quality_filter = filter_name)
  })

  # --- 5. Combine all results --------------------
  combined_results <- bind_rows(
    main_result %>% mutate(quality_filter = "All Studies"),
    main_rct_result %>% mutate(quality_filter = "All Studies"),
    sex_age_results %>% mutate(quality_filter = "All Studies"),
    quality_results
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      sex_group = factor(sex_group,
                         levels = c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female"))
    ) %>%
    arrange(quality_filter, sex_group, age_band)
  
  # --- 6. Create plots and tables for each sex group --------------------
  sex_groups <- c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female")
  quality_groups <- unique(combined_results$quality_filter)

  # Build integrated forest plots — 3 quality levels per age band, one plot per sex group
  # Colour = sex group (matching table row colours), Shape = quality filter
  sex_colours <- c(
    "main meta-analysis" = "springgreen3",
    "male" = "skyblue2",
    "female" = "indianred1"
  )

  quality_shapes <- c(
    "All Studies" = 16,
    "Low Risk of Bias Only" = 18,
    "Low + Moderate Risk of Bias" = 17
  )

  build_integrated_plots <- function() {
    plots <- purrr::map(sex_groups, function(sex) {
      sex_data <- combined_results %>%
        filter(sex_group == sex, !is.na(pooled_estimate))

      if (nrow(sex_data) == 0) {
        plot <- ggplot() + theme_void() +
          labs(title = str_to_title(sex))
        return(list(plot = plot, data = sex_data))
      }

      sex_col <- sex_colours[[sex]]

      plot <- sex_data %>%
        mutate(
          age_band = fct_rev(age_band),
          quality_filter = factor(quality_filter,
            levels = c("Low Risk of Bias Only", "Low + Moderate Risk of Bias", "All Studies"))
        ) %>%
        ggplot(aes(y = age_band, shape = quality_filter)) +
        geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_95, xmax = upper_95),
                       height = 0.2, colour = sex_col,
                       position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
        geom_point(aes(x = pooled_estimate), size = 3, colour = sex_col,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
        scale_shape_manual(
          values = quality_shapes,
          name = "Quality Filter"
        ) +
        labs(
          title = str_to_title(sex),
          x = "Estimated 95% CI",
          y = "Age Band"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
          plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.direction = "vertical",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
        )

      list(plot = plot, data = sex_data)
    })
    names(plots) <- sex_groups
    plots
  }

  output_list <- build_integrated_plots()
  
  # --- 7. Wald tests for comparisons --------------------

  # Helper: Wald test returning mean diff, 95% CI, % shift, and p-value
  wald_test <- function(mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2, ref_for_pct = NULL) {
    if (any(is.na(c(mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2)))) {
      return(list(diff = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_,
                  pct_shift = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
    }
    diff   <- mean1 - mean2
    se_dif <- sqrt(sd1^2 + sd2^2)
    lower  <- diff - 1.96 * se_dif
    upper  <- diff + 1.96 * se_dif
    z      <- diff / se_dif
    p      <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))
    ref    <- if (is.null(ref_for_pct)) mean2 else ref_for_pct
    pct    <- if (!is.na(ref) && ref != 0) 100 * diff / ref else NA_real_
    list(diff = diff, lower = lower, upper = upper, pct_shift = pct, p = p)
  }

  # Sex comparisons (Overall estimates — All Studies only)
  male_overall <- combined_results %>%
    filter(sex_group == "male", as.character(age_band) == "Overall", quality_filter == "All Studies")
  female_overall <- combined_results %>%
    filter(sex_group == "female", as.character(age_band) == "Overall", quality_filter == "All Studies")

  sex_w <- wald_test(male_overall$pooled_estimate,
                     female_overall$pooled_estimate,
                     male_overall$pooled_sd,
                     female_overall$pooled_sd)
  sex_comparison <- tibble(
    Comparison = "Male vs Female (Overall)",
    `Mean Difference` = sex_w$diff,
    `95% CI Lower`    = sex_w$lower,
    `95% CI Upper`    = sex_w$upper,
    `% Shift`         = sex_w$pct_shift,
    `P (Wald Test)`   = sex_w$p
  )

  # RCT vs All studies comparison (All Studies quality filter only)
  rct_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(sex_groups, function(sex) {
    all_studies <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex, as.character(age_band) == "Overall", quality_filter == "All Studies")
    rct_studies <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex, as.character(age_band) == "Overall (RCT only)", quality_filter == "All Studies")

    if (nrow(rct_studies) == 0 || is.na(rct_studies$pooled_estimate)) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    w <- wald_test(all_studies$pooled_estimate, rct_studies$pooled_estimate,
                   all_studies$pooled_sd,       rct_studies$pooled_sd)
    tibble(
      `Sex Group`        = sex,
      Comparison         = "All Studies vs RCT Only",
      `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
      `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
      `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
      `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
      `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
    )
  })

  # Age band comparisons within each sex group (All Studies only)
  age_band_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(sex_groups, function(sex) {
    sex_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex,
             quality_filter == "All Studies",
             as.character(age_band) != "Overall",
             as.character(age_band) != "Meta-Regression",
             !grepl("RCT only", as.character(age_band))) %>%
      arrange(age_band)

    if (nrow(sex_data) < 2) {
      return(tibble())
    }

    age_bands <- unique(as.character(sex_data$age_band))
    comparisons <- combn(age_bands, 2, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(comparisons, function(pair) {
      data1 <- sex_data %>% filter(as.character(age_band) == pair[1])
      data2 <- sex_data %>% filter(as.character(age_band) == pair[2])
      w <- wald_test(data1$pooled_estimate, data2$pooled_estimate,
                     data1$pooled_sd,       data2$pooled_sd)
      tibble(
        `Sex Group`        = sex,
        Comparison         = paste0(pair[1], " vs ", pair[2]),
        `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
        `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
        `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
        `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
        `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
      )
    })
  })

  # Sex comparison within each age band (All Studies only)
  age_band_sex_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_main, function(age) {
    male_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == "male", as.character(age_band) == as.character(age), quality_filter == "All Studies")
    female_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == "female", as.character(age_band) == as.character(age), quality_filter == "All Studies")

    if (nrow(male_data) == 0 || nrow(female_data) == 0) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    w <- wald_test(male_data$pooled_estimate, female_data$pooled_estimate,
                   male_data$pooled_sd,       female_data$pooled_sd)
    tibble(
      `Age Band`         = as.character(age),
      `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
      `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
      `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
      `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
      `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
    )
  })

  # Format all comparison tables — collapse diff + CI into one column,
  # show % shift (relative to the reference group), and the p-value.
  format_wald_table <- function(df) {
    if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
    n_rows <- nrow(df)

    df %>%
      mutate(
        `Mean Diff (95% CI)` = ifelse(
          is.na(`Mean Difference`), "—",
          sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", `Mean Difference`, `95% CI Lower`, `95% CI Upper`)
        ),
        `% Shift` = ifelse(is.na(`% Shift`), "—",
                           sprintf("%+.1f%%", `% Shift`)),
        `P (Wald Test)` = case_when(
          is.na(`P (Wald Test)`) ~ "—",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
          TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", `P (Wald Test)`)
        )
      ) %>%
      select(-`Mean Difference`, -`95% CI Lower`, -`95% CI Upper`) %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_align(align = "center", columns = everything()) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_fill(color = "#f7f7f7"),
        locations = cells_body(rows = seq(1, n_rows, by = 2))
      ) %>%
      tab_options(
        table.font.size = px(11),
        column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
        data_row.padding = px(3)
      ) %>%
      tab_source_note(
        md("*Mean difference = Group 1 − Group 2 in component units (mmol/24h, L/24h, or pH); % shift = difference relative to Group 2.*")
      )
  }
  
  sex_comparison_gt <- sex_comparison %>%
    format_wald_table() %>%
    tab_header(title = md("**Sex Comparison (Overall)**"))
  
  rct_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(rct_comparisons) > 0) {
    rct_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**All Studies vs RCT Only**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  age_band_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(age_band_comparisons) > 0) {
    age_band_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**Age Band Comparisons Within Sex Groups**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  age_band_sex_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(age_band_sex_comparisons) > 0) {
    age_band_sex_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**Sex Comparisons Within Age Bands**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  # --- 8. Create integrated wide-format summary table --------------------

  # Build wide table: one row per sex/age, columns per quality level
  all_quality_levels <- c("All Studies", "Low Risk of Bias Only", "Low + Moderate Risk of Bias")

  # Helper to format descriptive across-study summary
  fmt_desc <- function(avg, sdv, lo, hi) {
    if (is.na(avg) && is.na(lo) && is.na(hi)) return("\u2014")
    avg_part <- if (!is.na(avg) && !is.na(sdv)) sprintf("%.2f \u00b1 %.2f", avg, sdv) else "\u2014"
    rng_part <- if (!is.na(lo) && !is.na(hi))   sprintf("%.2f\u2013%.2f",  lo, hi)   else "\u2014"
    paste0(avg_part, " (", rng_part, ")")
  }

  # Ensure descriptive columns exist (meta-regression rows may not produce them)
  for (col in c("study_mean_avg", "study_mean_sd", "study_mean_min", "study_mean_max")) {
    if (!col %in% names(combined_results)) combined_results[[col]] <- NA_real_
  }

  wide_data <- combined_results %>%
    select(-urine_component) %>%
    mutate(
      quality_filter = ifelse(is.na(quality_filter), "All Studies", quality_filter),
      pooled_str = ifelse(
        is.na(pooled_estimate), "\u2014",
        sprintf("%.2f", pooled_estimate)
      ),
      ci_str = ifelse(
        is.na(lower_95) | is.na(upper_95), "\u2014",
        sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lower_95, upper_95)
      ),
      desc_str = mapply(fmt_desc, study_mean_avg, study_mean_sd, study_mean_min, study_mean_max),
      k_str = ifelse(is.na(n_studies) | n_studies == 0, "\u2014", as.character(n_studies))
    ) %>%
    select(sex_group, age_band, quality_filter, pooled_str, ci_str, desc_str, k_str, Q_pval, eggers_p) %>%
    distinct(sex_group, age_band, quality_filter, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    # Ensure all quality levels exist as columns even if no data
    complete(sex_group, age_band, quality_filter = all_quality_levels) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols = c(sex_group, age_band),
      names_from = quality_filter,
      values_from = c(pooled_str, ci_str, desc_str, k_str, Q_pval, eggers_p),
      names_glue = "{quality_filter}___{.value}"
    )

  fmt_pval <- function(p) {
    case_when(
      is.na(p) ~ "\u2014",
      p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
      p < 0.005 ~ "<0.005",
      p < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
      p < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", p)
    )
  }

  combined_summary_table <- wide_data %>%
    transmute(
      `Sex Group` = as.character(sex_group),
      `Age Band` = as.character(age_band),
      `Pooled (All)` = replace_na(`All Studies___pooled_str`, "\u2014"),
      `95% CI (All)` = replace_na(`All Studies___ci_str`, "\u2014"),
      `Studies Mean SD Range (All)` = replace_na(`All Studies___desc_str`, "\u2014"),

      `Studies Mean SD Range (Low)` = replace_na(`Low Risk of Bias Only___desc_str`, "\u2014"),
      `Studies, n (Low)` = replace_na(`Low Risk of Bias Only___k_str`, "\u2014"),
      `Q p (Low)` = fmt_pval(`Low Risk of Bias Only___Q_pval`),

      `Pooled (Low+Mod)` = replace_na(`Low + Moderate Risk of Bias___pooled_str`, "\u2014"),

      `Studies, n (Low+Mod)` = replace_na(`Low + Moderate Risk of Bias___k_str`, "\u2014"),
      `Q p (Low+Mod)` = fmt_pval(`Low + Moderate Risk of Bias___Q_pval`),
      `Egger's p (Low+Mod)` = fmt_pval(`Low + Moderate Risk of Bias___eggers_p`)
    )

  combined_summary_gt <- combined_summary_table %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Combined Meta-Analysis Results**"),
      subtitle = paste0("24-Hour Urine ", urine_component_for_title)
    ) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "All Studies", id = "spanner_all",
                columns = c(`Pooled (All)`, `95% CI (All)`, `Studies Mean SD Range (All)`,
                            `Studies, n (All)`, `Q p (All)`, `Egger's p (All)`)) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Low Risk of Bias Only", id = "spanner_low",
                columns = c(`Pooled (Low)`, `95% CI (Low)`, `Studies Mean SD Range (Low)`,
                            `Studies, n (Low)`, `Q p (Low)`, `Egger's p (Low)`)) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Low + Moderate RoB", id = "spanner_lowmod",
                columns = c(`Pooled (Low+Mod)`, `95% CI (Low+Mod)`, `Studies Mean SD Range (Low+Mod)`,
                            `Studies, n (Low+Mod)`, `Q p (Low+Mod)`, `Egger's p (Low+Mod)`)) %>%
    cols_label(
      `Pooled (All)` = "Pooled",
      `95% CI (All)` = "95% CI",
      `Studies Mean SD Range (All)` = md("Studies<br>Mean \u00b1 SD (Range)"),
      `Studies, n (All)` = "Studies, n",
      `Q p (All)` = "Q p-value",
      `Egger's p (All)` = "Egger's p",
      `Pooled (Low)` = "Pooled",
      `95% CI (Low)` = "95% CI",
      `Studies Mean SD Range (Low)` = md("Studies<br>Mean \u00b1 SD (Range)"),
      `Studies, n (Low)` = "Studies, n",
      `Q p (Low)` = "Q p-value",
      `Egger's p (Low)` = "Egger's p",
      `Pooled (Low+Mod)` = "Pooled",
      `95% CI (Low+Mod)` = "95% CI",
      `Studies Mean SD Range (Low+Mod)` = md("Studies<br>Mean \u00b1 SD (Range)"),
      `Studies, n (Low+Mod)` = "Studies, n",
      `Q p (Low+Mod)` = "Q p-value",

    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "center", columns = -c(`Sex Group`, `Age Band`)) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_spanners()
    ) %>%
    # Highlight by sex group — matching sex_age_race_subdivision_ma colours
    tab_style(

    )

  # --- 9. Create overall comparison plot (integrated quality) --------------------

  design <- "ABC
             EEE"

  # Row 1: Three integrated forest plots (all quality levels per plot)
```

## Comparison of Sex, Age and Race
```{r}
sex_age_race_subdivision_ma <- function(urine_component,
                                        data,
                                        overall_bias = NULL) {
  
  # --- 1. Identify the correct columns -------------------------------
  mean_colname <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "volume_mean_m_l",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "ph_mean",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "creatinine_mean_mmol_24h",
    TRUE ~ paste0(urine_component, "_mean_mmol_24h")
  )
  
  sd_colname <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "volume_sd_m_l",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "ph_sd",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "creatinine_sd_mmol_24h",
    TRUE ~ paste0(urine_component, "_sd_mmol_24h")
  )
  
  urine_component_for_title <- case_when(
    urine_component == "volume" ~ "Volume (L/24h)",
    urine_component == "ph" ~ "pH",
    urine_component == "creat" ~ "Creatinine (mmol/24h)",
    TRUE ~ paste0(str_to_title(urine_component), " (mmol/24h)")
  )
  
  # --- 2. Prepare data with overall_bias for meta-regression --------
  if (!is.null(overall_bias)) {
    data_with_bias <- data %>%
      left_join(overall_bias, by = "study_name")
  } else {
    data_with_bias <- data
  }
  
  # --- 3. Get main meta-analysis result ----------------------------
  # Overall main result (all sexes, all ages, all races)
  main_overall <- main_ma(urine_component, data = data) %>%
    mutate(sex_group = "main meta-analysis",
           age_band = "Overall",
           race_group = "All")
  
  # Main meta-analysis by age band (all sexes combined, all races)
  data_main <- data %>%
    select(
      study_name,
      total_n,
      age_band,
      mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
      sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname)
    ) %>%
    drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
  
  age_bands_main <- data_main %>% 
    filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>% 
    pull(age_band) %>% 
    unique() %>% 
    sort()
  
  main_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_main, function(age) {
    data_age <- data_main %>% 
      filter(age_band == age)
    
    if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    
    result <- run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, "main meta-analysis", age)
    result %>% mutate(race_group = "All")
  })
  
  # Add meta-regression for main analysis
  main_meta_reg_results <- tryCatch({
    result <- meta_regression("none", urine_component = urine_component)
    if (!is.null(result)) {
      result %>% mutate(race_group = "All")
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Meta-regression failed for main analysis: ", e$message)
    NULL
  })
  
  main_result <- bind_rows(main_overall, main_age_results, main_meta_reg_results)
  
  # --- 4. Iterate through sexes, age bands, and races ----------------------
  sex_age_race_results <- purrr::map_dfr(c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female"), function(sex) {
    
    # Filter data for this sex
    if (sex == "main meta-analysis") {
      data_sex <- data %>%
        select(
          study_name,
          total_n,
          age_band,
          race,
          mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
          sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
          study_type
        ) %>%
        drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
    } else {
      data_sex <- data %>% 
        filter(male_female == sex) %>%
        select(
          study_name,
          total_n,
          age_band,
          race,
          mean_col = all_of(mean_colname),
          sd_col   = all_of(sd_colname),
          study_type
        ) %>%
        drop_na(mean_col, sd_col)
    }
    
    if (nrow(data_sex) == 0) {
      return(tibble())
    }
    
    # Get overall result for this sex (all races)
    overall_result <- run_single_ma(data_sex, urine_component, sex, "Overall") %>%
      mutate(race_group = "All")
    
    # Get meta-regression result for this sex
    if (sex == "main meta-analysis") {
      meta_reg_result <- tryCatch({
        result <- meta_regression("none", urine_component = urine_component)
        if (!is.null(result)) {
          result %>% mutate(race_group = "All")
        } else {
          NULL
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        message("Meta-regression failed for ", sex, ": ", e$message)
        NULL
      })
    } else {
      meta_reg_result <- tryCatch({
        result <- meta_regression(data_subset = sex, urine_component = urine_component)
        if (!is.null(result)) {
          result %>% mutate(race_group = "All")
        } else {
          NULL
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        message("Meta-regression failed for ", sex, ": ", e$message)
        NULL
      })
    }
    
    # Get unique age bands
    age_bands <- data_sex %>% 
      filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>% 
      pull(age_band) %>% 
      unique() %>% 
      sort()
    
    # Get results for each age band (all races)
    age_band_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands, function(age) {
      data_age <- data_sex %>% 
        filter(age_band == age)
      
      if (nrow(data_age) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }
      
      result <- run_single_ma(data_age, urine_component, sex, age)
      result %>% mutate(race_group = "All")
    })
    
    # --- NEW: Race-specific analyses ---
    # Get unique race groups for this sex
    race_groups <- data_sex %>%
      filter(!is.na(race), race %in% c("white", "mixed", "black")) %>%
      pull(race) %>%
      unique() %>%
      sort()
    
    race_results <- purrr::map_dfr(race_groups, function(race) {
      data_race <- data_sex %>%
        filter(race == !!race)
      
      if (nrow(data_race) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }
      
      # Overall for this sex-race combination
      race_overall <- run_single_ma(data_race, urine_component, sex, "Overall") %>%
        mutate(race_group = race)
      
      # Age bands within this sex-race combination
      race_age_results <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands, function(age) {
        data_race_age <- data_race %>%
          filter(age_band == age)
        
        if (nrow(data_race_age) == 0) {
          return(tibble())
        }
        
        result <- run_single_ma(data_race_age, urine_component, sex, age)
        result %>% mutate(race_group = race)
      })
      
      bind_rows(race_overall, race_age_results)
    })
    
    # Combine all results for this sex
    bind_rows(overall_result, age_band_results, meta_reg_result, race_results)
  })
  
  # --- 5. Combine all results --------------------
  combined_results <- bind_rows(main_result, sex_age_race_results) %>%
    mutate(
      sex_group = factor(sex_group,
                        levels = c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female")),
      race_group = ifelse(is.na(race_group), "All", race_group)
    ) %>%
    arrange(sex_group, race_group, age_band)
  
  # Create complete grid to ensure all combinations are represented
  all_sex_groups <- c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female")
  all_race_groups <- c("All", "white", "mixed", "black")
  all_age_bands <- c("Overall", "Meta-Regression", sort(unique(combined_results$age_band[
    !combined_results$age_band %in% c("Overall", "Meta-Regression")
  ])))
  
  complete_grid <- expand.grid(
    sex_group = all_sex_groups,
    race_group = all_race_groups,
    age_band = all_age_bands,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    as_tibble()
  
  combined_results <- complete_grid %>%
    left_join(combined_results, by = c("sex_group", "race_group", "age_band")) %>%
    mutate(
      sex_group = factor(sex_group, levels = c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female"))
    ) %>%
    arrange(sex_group, race_group, age_band)
  
  # --- 6. Create plots for each sex group (All races) --------------------
  sex_groups <- c("main meta-analysis", "male", "female")
  
  output_list <- purrr::map(sex_groups, function(sex) {
    
    # Filter data for this sex group (All races only)
    sex_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex, race_group == "All")
    
    # Create forest plot
    colour <- case_when(
      sex == "main meta-analysis" ~ "springgreen3",
      sex == "male" ~ "skyblue2",
      sex == "female" ~ "indianred1"
    )
    
    plot <- sex_data %>%
      mutate(age_band = fct_rev(age_band)) %>%
      ggplot(aes(y = age_band)) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_95, xmax = upper_95), 
                     height = 0.25, colour = colour) +
      geom_point(aes(x = pooled_estimate), size = 3, colour = colour) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(str_to_title(sex)),
        x = "Estimated 95% CI",
        y = "Age Band"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
      )
    
    list(
      plot = plot,
      data = sex_data
    )
  })
  
  names(output_list) <- sex_groups
  
  # --- 7. Create race-specific plots for each sex --------------------
  # (Removed - now handled in section 11)
  
  # --- 8. Wald tests for comparisons --------------------

  # Helper: Wald test returning mean diff, 95% CI, % shift, and p-value
  wald_test <- function(mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2, ref_for_pct = NULL) {
    if (any(is.na(c(mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2)))) {
      return(list(diff = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_,
                  pct_shift = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
    }
    diff   <- mean1 - mean2
    se_dif <- sqrt(sd1^2 + sd2^2)
    lower  <- diff - 1.96 * se_dif
    upper  <- diff + 1.96 * se_dif
    z      <- diff / se_dif
    p      <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))
    ref    <- if (is.null(ref_for_pct)) mean2 else ref_for_pct
    pct    <- if (!is.na(ref) && ref != 0) 100 * diff / ref else NA_real_
    list(diff = diff, lower = lower, upper = upper, pct_shift = pct, p = p)
  }

  # Sex comparisons (Overall estimates, All races)
  male_overall <- combined_results %>%
    filter(sex_group == "male", as.character(age_band) == "Overall", race_group == "All")
  female_overall <- combined_results %>%
    filter(sex_group == "female", as.character(age_band) == "Overall", race_group == "All")

  sex_w <- wald_test(male_overall$pooled_estimate,   female_overall$pooled_estimate,
                     male_overall$pooled_sd,         female_overall$pooled_sd)
  sex_comparison <- tibble(
    Comparison        = "Male vs Female (Overall)",
    `Mean Difference` = sex_w$diff,
    `95% CI Lower`    = sex_w$lower,
    `95% CI Upper`    = sex_w$upper,
    `% Shift`         = sex_w$pct_shift,
    `P (Wald Test)`   = sex_w$p
  )

  # Race comparisons within each sex (Overall age band)
  race_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(c("male", "female"), function(sex) {
    race_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex, as.character(age_band) == "Overall",
             race_group != "All") %>%
      arrange(race_group)

    if (nrow(race_data) < 2) return(tibble())

    races <- unique(as.character(race_data$race_group))
    comparisons <- combn(races, 2, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(comparisons, function(pair) {
      data1 <- race_data %>% filter(race_group == pair[1])
      data2 <- race_data %>% filter(race_group == pair[2])
      w <- wald_test(data1$pooled_estimate, data2$pooled_estimate,
                     data1$pooled_sd,       data2$pooled_sd)
      tibble(
        `Sex Group`        = sex,
        Comparison         = paste0(pair[1], " vs ", pair[2]),
        `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
        `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
        `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
        `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
        `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
      )
    })
  })

  # Age band comparisons within each sex group (All races)
  age_band_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(sex_groups, function(sex) {
    sex_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex, race_group == "All",
             as.character(age_band) != "Overall",
             as.character(age_band) != "Meta-Regression") %>%
      arrange(age_band)

    if (nrow(sex_data) < 2) return(tibble())

    age_bands <- unique(as.character(sex_data$age_band))
    comparisons <- combn(age_bands, 2, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(comparisons, function(pair) {
      data1 <- sex_data %>% filter(as.character(age_band) == pair[1])
      data2 <- sex_data %>% filter(as.character(age_band) == pair[2])
      w <- wald_test(data1$pooled_estimate, data2$pooled_estimate,
                     data1$pooled_sd,       data2$pooled_sd)
      tibble(
        `Sex Group`        = sex,
        Comparison         = paste0(pair[1], " vs ", pair[2]),
        `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
        `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
        `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
        `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
        `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
      )
    })
  })

  # Sex comparison within each age band (All races)
  age_band_sex_comparisons <- purrr::map_dfr(age_bands_main, function(age) {
    male_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == "male", race_group == "All",
             as.character(age_band) == as.character(age))
    female_data <- combined_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == "female", race_group == "All",
             as.character(age_band) == as.character(age))

    if (nrow(male_data) == 0 || nrow(female_data) == 0) return(tibble())
    w <- wald_test(male_data$pooled_estimate, female_data$pooled_estimate,
                   male_data$pooled_sd,       female_data$pooled_sd)
    tibble(
      `Age Band`         = as.character(age),
      `Mean Difference`  = w$diff,
      `95% CI Lower`     = w$lower,
      `95% CI Upper`     = w$upper,
      `% Shift`          = w$pct_shift,
      `P (Wald Test)`    = w$p
    )
  })

  # Format all comparison tables — collapse diff + CI into one column,
  # show % shift (relative to the reference group), and the p-value.
  format_wald_table <- function(df) {
    if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
    n_rows <- nrow(df)
    df %>%
      mutate(
        `Mean Diff (95% CI)` = ifelse(
          is.na(`Mean Difference`), "—",
          sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", `Mean Difference`, `95% CI Lower`, `95% CI Upper`)
        ),
        `% Shift` = ifelse(is.na(`% Shift`), "—",
                           sprintf("%+.1f%%", `% Shift`)),
        `P (Wald Test)` = case_when(
          is.na(`P (Wald Test)`) ~ "—",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
          `P (Wald Test)` < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
          TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", `P (Wald Test)`)
        )
      ) %>%
      select(-`Mean Difference`, -`95% CI Lower`, -`95% CI Upper`) %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_align(align = "center", columns = everything()) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_fill(color = "#f7f7f7"),
        locations = cells_body(rows = seq(1, n_rows, by = 2))
      ) %>%
      tab_options(
        table.font.size = px(11),
        column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
        data_row.padding = px(3)
      ) %>%
      tab_source_note(
        md("*Mean difference = Group 1 − Group 2 in component units (mmol/24h, L/24h, or pH); % shift = difference relative to Group 2.*")
      )
  }

  sex_comparison_gt <- sex_comparison %>%
    format_wald_table() %>%
    tab_header(title = md("**Sex Comparison (Overall)**"))

  race_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(race_comparisons) > 0) {
    race_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**Race Comparisons Within Sex Groups**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  age_band_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(age_band_comparisons) > 0) {
    age_band_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**Age Band Comparisons Within Sex Groups**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  age_band_sex_comparisons_gt <- if (nrow(age_band_sex_comparisons) > 0) {
    age_band_sex_comparisons %>%
      format_wald_table() %>%
      tab_header(title = md("**Sex Comparisons Within Age Bands**"))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  # --- 9. Create combined summary table --------------------
  # Ensure descriptive columns exist (meta-regression rows may not produce them)
  for (col in c("study_mean_avg", "study_mean_sd", "study_mean_min", "study_mean_max")) {
    if (!col %in% names(combined_results)) combined_results[[col]] <- NA_real_
  }
  fmt_desc <- function(avg, sdv, lo, hi) {
    if (is.na(avg) && is.na(lo) && is.na(hi)) return("—")
    avg_part <- if (!is.na(avg) && !is.na(sdv)) sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", avg, sdv) else "—"
    rng_part <- if (!is.na(lo) && !is.na(hi))   sprintf("%.2f–%.2f",  lo, hi)   else "—"
    paste0(avg_part, " (", rng_part, ")")
  }

  combined_summary_table <- combined_results %>%
    select(-urine_component) %>%
    mutate(
      `Sex Group` = as.character(sex_group),
      `Race` = race_group,
      `Age Band` = as.character(age_band),
      `Pooled` = ifelse(is.na(pooled_estimate), "—", sprintf("%.2f", pooled_estimate)),
      `95% Range` = sprintf("%.2f – %.2f", lower_95, upper_95),
      `Studies Mean SD Range` = mapply(fmt_desc,
                                           study_mean_avg, study_mean_sd,
                                           study_mean_min, study_mean_max),
      Studies = n_studies,
      "Study Type" = study_type,
      Participants = total_participants,
      I2 = I2 * 100,
      `I²` = ifelse(is.na(I2), "—", paste0(round(I2, 1), "%")),
      `Cochran's Q` = ifelse(is.na(Q), "—", round(Q, 1)),
      `Q (p-value)` = case_when(
        is.na(Q_pval) ~ "—",
        Q_pval < 0.005 ~ "<0.005",
        Q_pval < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        Q_pval < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", Q_pval)
      ),
      `Egger's p` = case_when(
        is.na(eggers_p) ~ "—",
        eggers_p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        eggers_p < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        eggers_p < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", eggers_p)
      ),
      "Model" = model_utilised
    ) %>%
    select(
      `Sex Group`,
      `Race`,
      `Age Band`,
      `Pooled`,
      `95% Range`,
      `Studies Mean SD Range`,
      Studies,
      "Study Type",
      Participants,
      `I²`,
      `Cochran's Q`,
      `Q (p-value)`,
      `Egger's p`,
      Model
    )

  combined_summary_gt <- combined_summary_table %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Combined Meta-Analysis Results**"),
      subtitle = paste0("24-Hour Urine ", urine_component_for_title)
    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "center") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    # Highlight by sex group
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "springgreen3"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "main meta-analysis")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "skyblue2"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "male")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "indianred1"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "female")
    ) %>%
    # Bold the Overall rows
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = everything(),
        rows = `Age Band` == "Overall"
      )
    ) %>%
    # Bold and highlight Meta-Regression rows
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = everything(),
        rows = `Age Band` == "Meta-Regression"
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(11),
      heading.title.font.size = px(14),
      heading.subtitle.font.size = px(12),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      data_row.padding = px(3)
    ) %>%
    tab_source_note(
      source_note = md("*I² represents heterogeneity; Q test assesses between-study variation; Egger's p = linear regression test for funnel plot asymmetry; Meta-Regression shows covariate-adjusted estimates*")
    )

  # --- 10. Create overall comparison plot (Age-stratified) --------------------
  
  design <- "ABC
             EEE"
  
  # Row 1: Three forest plots 
  row1 <- (
      output_list[["main meta-analysis"]]$plot |
        output_list[["male"]]$plot |
        output_list[["female"]]$plot 
    )
  
  # Row 2: Combined summary table
  row2 <- wrap_elements(full = combined_summary_gt) 
  
  # Combine rows
  final_layout <- row1 + row2 + 
    plot_layout(design = design,
                axis_titles = "collect",
                axes = "collect") + 
    plot_annotation(
      title = urine_component_for_title,
      tag_levels = "A",
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
    )
  
  # --- 11. Create race-stratified plot and table --------------------
  
  # Filter for white, mixed, and black races (including All)
  race_results <- combined_results %>%
    filter(race_group %in% c("All", "white", "mixed", "black"))
  
  # Create race-only summary table (separate from combined table)
  race_only_summary_table <- race_results %>%
    filter(race_group != "All") %>%  # Exclude "All" for race-specific table
    select(-urine_component) %>%
    mutate(
      `Sex Group` = as.character(sex_group),
      `Race` = str_to_title(race_group),
      `Age Band` = as.character(age_band),
      `95% Range` = ifelse(
        is.na(lower_95) | is.na(upper_95),
        "—",
        sprintf("%.2f – %.2f", lower_95, upper_95)
      ),
      Studies = ifelse(is.na(n_studies), "—", as.character(n_studies)),
      "Study Type" = study_type,
      Participants = ifelse(is.na(total_participants), "—", as.character(total_participants)),
      I2_val = I2 * 100,
      `I²` = ifelse(is.na(I2_val), "—", paste0(round(I2_val, 1), "%")),
      `Cochran's Q` = ifelse(is.na(Q), "—", as.character(round(Q, 1))),
      `Q (p-value)` = case_when(
        is.na(Q_pval) ~ "—",
        Q_pval < 0.005 ~ "<0.005",
        Q_pval < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        Q_pval < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", Q_pval)
      ),
      `Egger's p` = case_when(
        is.na(eggers_p) ~ "—",
        eggers_p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        eggers_p < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        eggers_p < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", eggers_p)
      ),
      "Model" = ifelse(is.na(model_utilised), "—", model_utilised)
    ) %>%
    select(
      `Sex Group`,
      `Race`,
      `Age Band`,
      `95% Range`,
      Studies,
      "Study Type",
      Participants,
      `I²`,
      `Cochran's Q`,
      `Q (p-value)`,
      `Egger's p`,
      Model
    )

  race_only_summary_gt <- race_only_summary_table %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Race-Specific Meta-Analysis Results**"),
      subtitle = paste0("24-Hour Urine ", urine_component_for_title)
    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "center") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    # Highlight by sex group
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "springgreen3"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "main meta-analysis")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "skyblue2"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "male")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "indianred1"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "female")
    ) %>%
    # Bold the Overall rows
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = everything(),
        rows = `Age Band` == "Overall"
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(11),
      heading.title.font.size = px(14),
      heading.subtitle.font.size = px(12),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      data_row.padding = px(3)
    ) %>%
    tab_source_note(
      source_note = md("*I² represents heterogeneity; Q test assesses between-study variation; Egger's p = linear regression test for funnel plot asymmetry; — indicates insufficient data*")
    )

  # Create forest plots by sex for race stratification
  race_output_list <- purrr::map(sex_groups, function(sex) {
    
    # Filter data for this sex group
    sex_race_data <- race_results %>%
      filter(sex_group == sex) %>%
      mutate(
        # Create a combined label for plotting
        plot_label = case_when(
          race_group == "All" & age_band == "Overall" ~ "Overall (All Races)",
          race_group == "All" & age_band == "Meta-Regression" ~ "Meta-Regression (All Races)",
          race_group == "All" ~ paste0(age_band, " (All Races)"),
          age_band == "Overall" ~ str_to_title(race_group),
          age_band == "Meta-Regression" ~ paste0(str_to_title(race_group), " - Meta-Regression"),
          TRUE ~ paste0(str_to_title(race_group), " - ", age_band)
        ),
        # Order for plotting
        plot_order = case_when(
          race_group == "All" & age_band == "Overall" ~ 1,
          race_group == "All" & age_band == "Meta-Regression" ~ 2,
          race_group == "white" & age_band == "Overall" ~ 3,
          race_group == "mixed" & age_band == "Overall" ~ 4,
          race_group == "black" & age_band == "Overall" ~ 5,
          TRUE ~ 6 + row_number()
        )
      ) %>%
      arrange(plot_order)
    
    if (nrow(sex_race_data) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Create forest plot
    colour <- case_when(
      sex == "main meta-analysis" ~ "springgreen3",
      sex == "male" ~ "skyblue2",
      sex == "female" ~ "indianred1"
    )
    
    # Only plot rows with non-NA estimates
    sex_race_data_plot <- sex_race_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(pooled_estimate))
    
    plot <- sex_race_data_plot %>%
      mutate(plot_label = fct_reorder(plot_label, -plot_order)) %>%
      ggplot(aes(y = plot_label)) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_95, xmax = upper_95), 
                     height = 0.25, colour = colour) +
      geom_point(aes(x = pooled_estimate), size = 3, colour = colour) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(str_to_title(sex)),
        x = "Estimated 95% CI",
        y = NULL
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9)
      )
    
    list(
      plot = plot,
      data = sex_race_data
    )
  })
  
  names(race_output_list) <- sex_groups
  
  # Create race summary table (with All races for the plot)
  race_summary_table <- race_results %>%
    select(-urine_component) %>%
    mutate(
      `Sex Group` = as.character(sex_group),
      `Race` = case_when(
        race_group == "All" ~ "All Races",
        TRUE ~ str_to_title(race_group)
      ),
      `Age Band` = as.character(age_band),
      `95% Range` = ifelse(
        is.na(lower_95) | is.na(upper_95),
        "—",
        sprintf("%.2f – %.2f", lower_95, upper_95)
      ),
      Studies = ifelse(is.na(n_studies), "—", as.character(n_studies)),
      "Study Type" = study_type,
      Participants = ifelse(is.na(total_participants), "—", as.character(total_participants)),
      I2_val = I2 * 100,
      `I²` = ifelse(is.na(I2_val), "—", paste0(round(I2_val, 1), "%")),
      `Cochran's Q` = ifelse(is.na(Q), "—", as.character(round(Q, 1))),
      `Q (p-value)` = case_when(
        is.na(Q_pval) ~ "—",
        Q_pval < 0.005 ~ "<0.005",
        Q_pval < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        Q_pval < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", Q_pval)
      ),
      `Egger's p` = case_when(
        is.na(eggers_p) ~ "—",
        eggers_p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        eggers_p < 0.01  ~ "<0.01",
        eggers_p < 0.05  ~ "<0.05",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f", eggers_p)
      ),
      "Model" = ifelse(is.na(model_utilised), "—", model_utilised)
    ) %>%
    select(
      `Sex Group`,
      `Race`,
      `Age Band`,
      `95% Range`,
      Studies,
      "Study Type",
      Participants,
      `I²`,
      `Cochran's Q`,
      `Q (p-value)`,
      `Egger's p`,
      Model
    )

  race_summary_gt <- race_summary_table %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Race-Stratified Meta-Analysis Results**"),
      subtitle = paste0("24-Hour Urine ", urine_component_for_title)
    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "center") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    # Highlight by sex group
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "springgreen3"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "main meta-analysis")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "skyblue2"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "male")
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "indianred1"),
      locations = cells_body(rows = `Sex Group` == "female")
    ) %>%
    # Bold the Overall rows
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = everything(),
        rows = `Age Band` == "Overall"
      )
    ) %>%
    # Bold the "All Races" rows
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = everything(),
        rows = `Race` == "All Races"
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(11),
      heading.title.font.size = px(14),
      heading.subtitle.font.size = px(12),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      data_row.padding = px(3)
    ) %>%
    tab_source_note(
      source_note = md("*I² represents heterogeneity; Q test assesses between-study variation; Egger's p = linear regression test for funnel plot asymmetry; — indicates insufficient data*")
    )

  # Create race comparison plot layout
  race_row1 <- (
      race_output_list[["main meta-analysis"]]$plot |
        race_output_list[["male"]]$plot |
        race_output_list[["female"]]$plot 
    )
  
  race_row2 <- wrap_elements(full = race_summary_gt)
  
  race_layout <- race_row1 + race_row2 + 
    plot_layout(design = design,
                axis_titles = "collect",
                axes = "collect") + 
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(urine_component_for_title, " - Race Stratification"),
      tag_levels = "A",
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
    )
  
  # --- 12. Return results --------------------
  return(list(
    ma_results = combined_results,
    main_meta_analysis = output_list[["main meta-analysis"]],
    male = output_list[["male"]],
    female = output_list[["female"]],
    combined_plot = final_layout,
    combined_summary_table = combined_summary_gt,
    race_plot = race_layout,
    race_summary_table = race_summary_gt,
    race_only_table = race_only_summary_gt,
    wald_tests = list(
      sex_comparison = sex_comparison_gt,
      race_comparisons = race_comparisons_gt,
      age_band_comparisons = age_band_comparisons_gt,
      sex_within_age_bands = age_band_sex_comparisons_gt
    )
  ))
}
```

# Bias Analysis {.tabset .tabset-pills}
## Observational Studies 
```{r}
bias_observational_table <- bias_observational %>%
  rename_with(~str_remove(., "_low_moderate_high"), everything()) %>%
  arrange(study) %>%
  rename(
    Study = study,
    `Study Participation` = study_participation,
    `Study Attrition` = study_attrition,
    `Prognostic Factor Measurement` = prognostic_factor_measurement,
    `Outcomes Measurement` = outcomes_measurement,
    `Study Confounding` = study_confounding,
    `Statistical Analysis` = statistical_analysis,
    Overall = overall
  )

bias_observational_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Risk of Bias Assessment for Observational Studies"
  ) %>%
  # Color coding function
  data_color(
    columns = c(`Study Participation`, `Study Attrition`, `Prognostic Factor Measurement`,
                `Outcomes Measurement`, `Study Confounding`, `Statistical Analysis`, Overall),
    fn = function(x) {
      case_when(
        x == "Low" ~ "#90EE90",     
        x == "Moderate" ~ "#FFD700",  
        x == "High" ~ "#FF6B6B",      
        TRUE ~ "#FFFFFF"              
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Overall)
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(`Study Participation`, `Study Attrition`, `Prognostic Factor Measurement`,
                `Outcomes Measurement`, `Study Confounding`, `Statistical Analysis`, Overall)
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = Study
  ) %>%
  opt_row_striping()
```
\newpage

## RCTs
```{r}
bias_rcts_table <- bias_rcts %>%
  mutate(
    risk_of_bias_in_selection_of_reported_result_low_some_concern_high = case_when(
      risk_of_bias_in_selection_of_reported_result_low_some_concern_high == "Low" ~ "Low",
      risk_of_bias_in_selection_of_reported_result_low_some_concern_high == "Some Concern" ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE ~ "Low"
    )
  ) %>%
  rename_with(~str_remove(., "_low_some_concern_high"), everything()) %>%
  arrange(study) %>%
  rename(
    Study = study,
    `Randomisation` = risk_of_bias_from_randomising_process,
    `Deviations from Intended Intervention Effect - Assignment` = risk_of_bias_due_to_deviations_from_the_intended_interventions_effect_of_assingment_to_intervention,
    `Deviations from Intended Intervention Effect - Adherence` = risk_of_bias_due_to_deviations_from_the_intended_interventions_effect_of_adhering_to_intervention,
    
    `Missing Outcomes` = missing_outcome_data,
    `Measurement of Outcome` = risk_of_bias_in_measurement_of_outcome,
    `Selection of Reported Result` = risk_of_bias_in_selection_of_reported_result,
    Overall = overall
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(-Study, ~str_replace_all(., "Some concern", "Moderate")),
         across(-Study, ~str_replace_all(., "Low ", "Low")),
         across(-Study, ~str_replace_all(., "Some Concern", "Moderate")))

bias_rcts_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Risk of Bias Assessment for Randomised Controlled Studies"
  ) %>%
  # Color coding function
  data_color(
    columns = c(`Randomisation`, `Deviations from Intended Intervention Effect - Assignment`, `Deviations from Intended Intervention Effect - Adherence`,
                `Missing Outcomes`, `Measurement of Outcome`, `Selection of Reported Result`, Overall),
    fn = function(x) {
      case_when(
        x == "Low" ~ "#90EE90",     
        x == "Moderate" ~ "#FFD700",  
        x == "High" ~ "#FF6B6B",      
        TRUE ~ "#FFFFFF"              
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Overall)
```

# GRADE {.tabset .tabset-pills}
## Function to Derive GRADE rating
```{r}
calculate_grade <- function(study_design, 
                           risk_of_bias, 
                           inconsistency, 
                           indirectness, 
                           imprecision, 
                           publication_bias,
                           large_effect = FALSE,
                           dose_response = FALSE,
                           confounders_reduce_effect = FALSE) {
  
  # Starting point based on study design
  if (study_design == "RCT") {
    certainty <- 4  # High
  } else if (study_design == "Observational" | study_design == "Mixed") {
    certainty <- 2  # Low
  } else {
    certainty <- 1  # Very Low
  }
  
  # Downgrade for limitations
  if (risk_of_bias == "Serious") certainty <- certainty - 1
  if (risk_of_bias == "Very serious") certainty <- certainty - 2
  
  if (inconsistency == "Serious") certainty <- certainty - 1
  if (inconsistency == "Very serious") certainty <- certainty - 2
  
  if (indirectness == "Serious") certainty <- certainty - 1
  if (indirectness == "Very serious") certainty <- certainty - 2
  
  if (imprecision == "Serious") certainty <- certainty - 1
  if (imprecision == "Very serious") certainty <- certainty - 2
  
  if (publication_bias == "Strongly suspected") certainty <- certainty - 1
  
  # Upgrade for observational studies
  if (study_design == "Observational" | study_design == "Mixed") {
    if (large_effect) certainty <- certainty + 1
    if (dose_response) certainty <- certainty + 1
    if (confounders_reduce_effect) certainty <- certainty + 1
  }
  
  # Ensure certainty stays within bounds
  certainty <- max(1, min(4, certainty))
  
  # Convert to GRADE rating
  grade_rating <- case_when(
    certainty == 4 ~ "High",
    certainty == 3 ~ "Moderate",
    certainty == 2 ~ "Low",
    certainty == 1 ~ "Very Low"
  )
  
  return(list(
    certainty_score = certainty,
    grade_rating = grade_rating
  ))
}

# Function to create GRADE quality symbols
grade_symbol <- function(grade_rating) {
  symbols <- case_when(
    grade_rating == "High" | grade_rating == 4 ~ "⊕⊕⊕⊕",
    grade_rating == "Moderate" | grade_rating == 3 ~ "⊕⊕⊕◯",
    grade_rating == "Low" | grade_rating == 2 ~ "⊕⊕◯◯",
    grade_rating == "Very Low" | grade_rating == 1 ~ "⊕◯◯◯",
    TRUE ~ "◯◯◯◯"
  )
  return(symbols)
}

# Helper for the GRADE `confounders_reduce_effect` upgrade.
# Returns TRUE when EITHER:
#   (a) meta-regression R² > 25% (substantial heterogeneity explained), OR
#   (b) meta-regression pooled estimate differs from overall pooled by ≥ 5%
#       (regression-adjusted result is meaningfully different from unadjusted)
# `ma_results` is the standard *_ma_2nd_analysis$ma_results data frame.
mr_reduces_effect <- function(ma_results,
                              R2_threshold      = 0.25,
                              shift_threshold   = 0.05) {
  ov <- ma_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(sex_group == "main meta-analysis",
                  age_band == "Overall",
                  quality_filter == "All Studies")
  mr <- ma_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(sex_group == "main meta-analysis",
                  age_band == "Meta-Regression",
                  quality_filter == "All Studies")

  if (!nrow(ov) || !nrow(mr)) return(FALSE)

  # Rule (a): high R² alone is sufficient
  R2 <- if ("R2" %in% names(mr)) mr$R2[1] else NA_real_
  if (!is.na(R2) && R2 > R2_threshold) return(TRUE)

  # Rule (b): MR pooled meaningfully different from overall pooled
  ov_est <- ov$pooled_estimate[1]
  mr_est <- mr$pooled_estimate[1]
  if (is.na(ov_est) || is.na(mr_est) || ov_est == 0) return(FALSE)
  rel_diff <- abs(mr_est - ov_est) / abs(ov_est)
  rel_diff >= shift_threshold
}
```


# Finalised Results {.tabset .tabset-pills}
## Functions
### Function to get final result
```{r}
get_final_ma_results <- function(ma_results, sex_specific = FALSE, meta_regression = FALSE, low_rob = FALSE) {
  if (sex_specific) {
    ma_results %>% filter(age_band == "Overall", sex_group != "main meta-analysis",
                          quality_filter == "All Studies")
  } else if (meta_regression) {
    ma_results %>% filter(age_band == "Meta-Regression", sex_group == "main meta-analysis", quality_filter == "All Studies")
  } else if (low_rob) {
    ma_results %>% filter(age_band == "Overall", sex_group == "main meta-analysis", quality_filter == "Low Risk of Bias Only")
  } else {
    ma_results %>% filter(sex_group == "main meta-analysis", age_band == "Overall",
                          quality_filter == "All Studies")
  }
}
```

## Recommendations Summary

This summary applies the decision framework defined earlier (see *Flow Diagram
detailing Decision Making*) to each urine component using the per-component
meta-analysis objects (`*_ma_2nd_analysis` and `*_ma_3rd_analysis`). It is
placed here, at the top of the Finalised Results, so the reader can see
**which outcome was selected for which component and why** before reading the
per-component conclusions below.

```{r applied_recommendations_final}
# Pull together rows from the *_ma_2nd_analysis$ma_results outputs
all_ma_long <- purrr::map_dfr(analysis_components, function(comp) {
  obj_name <- paste0(comp, "_ma_2nd_analysis")
  if (!exists(obj_name)) return(tibble::tibble())
  obj <- get(obj_name)
  if (is.null(obj$ma_results)) return(tibble::tibble())
  res <- obj$ma_results
  if (!"urine_component" %in% names(res)) res$urine_component <- comp
  if (!"quality_filter" %in% names(res))  res$quality_filter  <- "All Studies"
  res
})

# Guard: if no per-component objects are loaded yet, render a placeholder
if (nrow(all_ma_long) == 0) {
  gt::gt(tibble::tibble(
    Message = "No *_ma_2nd_analysis objects found — re-run all per-component sections first."
  ))
} else {
  all_ma_long <- all_ma_long %>%
    dplyr::mutate(age_band  = tolower(as.character(age_band)),
                  sex_group = tolower(as.character(sex_group)))

  # Build race-stratified long table from *_ma_3rd_analysis (for Q4)
  all_ma_race_long <- purrr::map_dfr(analysis_components, function(comp) {
    obj_name <- paste0(comp, "_ma_3rd_analysis")
    if (!exists(obj_name)) return(tibble::tibble())
    obj <- get(obj_name)
    if (is.null(obj$ma_results)) return(tibble::tibble())
    res <- obj$ma_results
    if (!"urine_component" %in% names(res)) res$urine_component <- comp
    res
  })

  # Build long-format meta-regression coefficient table from the global
  # `meta_reg_full_results` cache populated by meta_regression(). Used by
  # Bridge 1 (women_prop_c coefficient) and Bridge 4 (R² for Q6).
  all_meta_reg_long <- if (exists("meta_reg_full_results") &&
                            length(meta_reg_full_results) > 0) {
    purrr::map_dfr(names(meta_reg_full_results), function(key) {
      tbl <- meta_reg_full_results[[key]]
      if (is.null(tbl) || !nrow(tbl)) return(tibble::tibble())
      parts <- strsplit(key, "__", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      tbl %>% dplyr::mutate(urine_component = parts[1],
                             sex_group       = parts[2])
    })
  } else NULL

  # Apply the integrated framework
  recommendations <- purrr::map_dfr(analysis_components, function(comp) {
    tryCatch(
      recommend_analysis(comp,
                         ma_long       = all_ma_long,
                         ma_race_long  = all_ma_race_long,
                         data          = urine_ma2,
                         meta_reg_long = all_meta_reg_long),
      error = function(e) tibble::tibble(component = comp,
                                          outcome  = "ERROR",
                                          branch   = NA_character_,
                                          reason   = e$message)
    )
  })

  recommendations %>%
    dplyr::mutate(component = stringr::str_to_title(component),
                  R2 = ifelse(is.na(R2), "—", sprintf("%.1f%%", R2 * 100)),
                  k  = ifelse(is.na(k), "—", as.character(k)),
                  n  = ifelse(is.na(n), "—", format(n, big.mark = ","))) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      `Sex p (women_prop / overall / MR / LRoB)` =
        paste(format_p(p_women_prop %||% NA_real_),
              format_p(p_sex_overall),
              format_p(p_sex_metareg),
              format_p(p_sex_lowrob), sep = " / "),
      `Age p (min)`   = format_p(p_age),
      `Race p (min)`  = format_p(p_race),
      `Assay p (min)` = format_p(p_assay),
      `Egger's p`     = format_p(eggers_p %||% NA_real_),
      # Quality-gate display: Cochran's Q normalised by df, MR R² for chosen subset
      `Q/df (chosen / overall)` = paste0(
        ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_chosen),  "—", sprintf("%.1f", qc_q_ratio_chosen)),
        " / ",
        ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_overall), "—", sprintf("%.1f", qc_q_ratio_overall))
      ),
      `Q/df ratio (chosen÷overall)` = ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_rel), "—",
                                              sprintf("%.2f", qc_q_ratio_rel)),
      `Q p (chosen)` = format_p(qc_q_pval_chosen),
      `MR R² (chosen)` = ifelse(is.na(qc_mr_R2_chosen), "—",
                                 sprintf("%.0f%%", qc_mr_R2_chosen * 100)),
      `QC warnings` = ifelse(qc_warnings == "" | is.na(qc_warnings), "—", qc_warnings)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(Component = component,
                  k, n, `R²` = R2,
                  `Sex p (women_prop / overall / MR / LRoB)`,
                  `Age p (min)`,
                  `Race p (min)`,
                  `Assay p (min)`,
                  `Egger's p`,
                  `Q/df (chosen / overall)`,
                  `Q/df ratio (chosen÷overall)`,
                  `Q p (chosen)`,
                  `MR R² (chosen)`,
                  `Recommended Analysis` = outcome,
                  Branch  = branch,
                  Rationale = reason,
                  `QC warnings`) %>%
    gt::gt() %>%
    gt::tab_header(
      title    = gt::md("**Decision-Framework Recommendations per Urine Component**"),
      subtitle = gt::md(sprintf(
        "Q1 data → Q2 sex → Q3 age → Q4 race → Q5 assay → Q6 meta-reg (R²) → Q6b meta-reg (Egger's) → Q6c meta-reg (no stratum effect + valid range) → Q7 low-RoB → Q8 overall pooled. Thresholds: k≥%d, n≥%d, R²≥%.0f%% (Q6) or ≥%.0f%% (Q6c) & k≥%d, Wald p<%.2f, Egger p<%.2f, consistency ≤%.0f%%.",
        THRESHOLDS$k_min, THRESHOLDS$n_min,
        THRESHOLDS$R2_min * 100, THRESHOLDS$R2_q6c_min * 100, THRESHOLDS$R2_k_min, THRESHOLDS$wald_alpha,
        THRESHOLDS$eggers_alpha,
        THRESHOLDS$consistency_pct * 100))
    ) %>%
    gt::data_color(
      columns = `Recommended Analysis`,
      fn = function(x) {
        dplyr::case_when(
          x == "Sex-stratified"             ~ "#cce5ff",
          x == "Age-stratified"             ~ "#cff4fc",
          x == "Race-stratified"            ~ "#d1e7dd",
          x == "Assay/country-stratified"   ~ "#cfe2ff",
          x == "Meta-regression"            ~ "#d4edda",
          x == "Low risk-of-bias overall"   ~ "#e2d4f0",
          x == "Overall pooled (caveats)"   ~ "#f8d7da",
          x == "Overall pooled"             ~ "#ffe5d0",
          TRUE                               ~ "#f0f0f0"
        )
      }
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 10, data_row.padding = gt::px(4))
}
```

### Framework Recommendation Helper

```{r framework_callout_helper}
# Render a one-row "Framework Recommendation" callout for a single component.
# Pulls from the global `recommendations` tibble built above.
framework_callout <- function(component_code) {
  if (!exists("recommendations") || !inherits(recommendations, "data.frame") ||
      nrow(recommendations) == 0) {
    return(gt::gt(tibble::tibble(
      Message = "Framework not yet computed — see Recommendations Summary."
    )))
  }
  rec <- recommendations %>%
    dplyr::filter(tolower(component) == tolower(component_code))
  if (nrow(rec) == 0) {
    return(gt::gt(tibble::tibble(
      Message = sprintf("No framework recommendation for %s", component_code)
    )))
  }
  rec %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Component   = component,
      Recommended = outcome,
      Branch      = branch,
      Reason      = reason,
      k = ifelse(is.na(k), "—", as.character(k)),
      n = ifelse(is.na(n), "—", format(n, big.mark = ",")),
      `R²` = ifelse(is.na(R2), "—", sprintf("%.1f%%", R2 * 100)),
      `Sex p (women_prop / overall / MR / LRoB)` =
        paste(format_p(p_women_prop %||% NA_real_),
              format_p(p_sex_overall),
              format_p(p_sex_metareg),
              format_p(p_sex_lowrob), sep = " / "),
      `Age p (min)`   = format_p(p_age),
      `Race p (min)`  = format_p(p_race),
      `Assay p (min)` = format_p(p_assay),
      `Egger's p`     = format_p(eggers_p %||% NA_real_),
      `Q/df (chosen / overall)` = paste0(
        ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_chosen),  "—", sprintf("%.1f", qc_q_ratio_chosen)),
        " / ",
        ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_overall), "—", sprintf("%.1f", qc_q_ratio_overall))
      ),
      `Q/df ratio (chosen÷overall)` = ifelse(is.na(qc_q_ratio_rel), "—",
                                              sprintf("%.2f", qc_q_ratio_rel)),
      `Q p (chosen)` = format_p(qc_q_pval_chosen),
      `MR R² (chosen)` = ifelse(is.na(qc_mr_R2_chosen), "—",
                                 sprintf("%.0f%%", qc_mr_R2_chosen * 100)),
      `QC warnings` = ifelse(qc_warnings == "" | is.na(qc_warnings),
                             "—", qc_warnings)
    ) %>%
    gt::gt() %>%
    gt::tab_header(
      title    = gt::md(sprintf("**Framework Recommendation — %s**", rec$component)),
      subtitle = gt::md(sprintf("Branch %s", rec$branch))
    ) %>%
    gt::data_color(
      columns = Recommended,
      fn = function(x) {
        dplyr::case_when(
          x == "Sex-stratified"             ~ "#cce5ff",
          x == "Age-stratified"             ~ "#cff4fc",
          x == "Race-stratified"            ~ "#d1e7dd",
          x == "Assay/country-stratified"   ~ "#cfe2ff",
          x == "Meta-regression"            ~ "#d4edda",
          x == "Low risk-of-bias overall"   ~ "#e2d4f0",
          x == "Overall pooled (caveats)"   ~ "#f8d7da",
          x == "Overall pooled"             ~ "#ffe5d0",
          TRUE                               ~ "#f0f0f0"
        )
      }
    ) %>%
    gt::cols_align(align = "center", columns = -c(Component, Reason)) %>%
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 11, data_row.padding = gt::px(4))
}
```

## Volume {.tabset .tabset-pills}
### Framework Recommendation
```{r volume_framework_callout}
framework_callout("volume")
```

### Comment
There is high heterogeneity throughout the analyses. Age consistently shifts the distribution, although differences between age bands are non-significant. There seem to be some minor differences between sexes, but again these are non significant.<br>
The race-specific estimates are underpowered and unstable – many are single studies or have implausibly wide ranges. On Wald tests: The only between group differences that were significant were black (1.40-1.75, n=304, I2=60%) vs white women (1.76-2.05, n=3260, I2=78%), and all races (0.94-2.40, n=4177, I2=99%) vs white women. In the meta-regression of women only, there is a significant decrease in the lower limit (from 0.94 in main MA to 0.55). <br>
Meta-regression shows significantly higher volumes in small studies and does not explain the observed heterogeneity with an R2 = 9.9%. The extreme heterogeneity is largely unexplained by age, sex, study quality, or sample size, although there appears to be a small study effect. The RCT only analyses are limited by small sample sizes, but the lower limit (~1L) seems consistent across analyses. <br>
**Framework recommendation: Overall pooled meta-analysis.** Meta-regression R² of 7.6% is below the 25% threshold for explained heterogeneity and Egger’s test (p=0.811) does not detect small-study bias, so the simpler unadjusted pooled estimate is preferred.
<br>

## Calcium {.tabset .tabset-pills}
### Framework Recommendation
```{r calcium_framework_callout}
framework_callout("calcium")
```

### Comment
There is extremely high heterogeneity throughout the analyses. Meta-regression does not narrow this difference and therefore the variability is likely due to structural differences between studies. Age and Sex appear to affect the distribution of results. Race analyses are much less robust with single studies, negative values and substantial heterogeneity. However, each of the subanalyses are severely underpowered with small numbers of studies and patients. The RCT subanalyses demonstrate tighter intervals than the other analyses, however, there are far fewer patients and this is not likely to be representative of the wider population. <br>
	We therefore suggest using the **meta-regression result** as this accounts for ~ 36% of heterogeneity (R2 = 36%). It should be noted that there is substantial heterogeneity and therefore uncertainty in the results. These figures should not be used as a precise expected range.

<br>

## Urate {.tabset .tabset-pills}
### Framework Recommendation
```{r urate_framework_callout}
framework_callout("urate")
```

### Comment
Most ranges lie between ~2-5mmol/24h. There is high heterogeneity, and meta-regression modestly narrows the range, suggesting a central tendency. Age seems to slightly modify spread but not location of the range. There appear to be differences between sexes, although these are not significant and the analyses appear to be underpowered. Race analyses are underpowered with mostly single studies and wide ranges. No differences on Wald tests. On meta-regression of the overall dataset, the model did not account for any heterogeneity (R2 = 0%), and the only significant difference was between the sexes (for women: -0.77 mmol/24h, p=0.024). The RCT subanalyses have results within the respective ranges of the other analyses. The wider spread of the other analyses suggests they are more representative of the wider population. <br>
	We therefore suggest using **sex-stratified main results**. It should be noted that there were substantially fewer male participants, and this result should be interpreted with caution.
<br>

### Framework Recommendation
```{r creat_framework_callout}
framework_callout("creat")
```

### Comment
There is substantial heterogeneity in all analyses. There are clear and significant differences between sexes and age-bands. However, age stratification dramatically reduces the number of eligible studies and reduces the number of participants, reducing the power of these analyses. Race sub-analyses are underpowered with mostly single studies and wide ranges. Meta-regression suggests that women have significantly lower values than men. <br>
	Could potentially use **sex stratified ranges** only as observed adult population distributions.

## Oxalate {.tabset .tabset-pills}
### Framework Recommendation
```{r oxalate_framework_callout}
framework_callout("oxalate")
```

### Comment
There is significant variation across age, sex and race analyses along with high heterogeneity in most categories, save for some subgroups. These subgroups tend to be limited to small datasets with a small number of studies. The main analysis meta-regression demonstrates a significantly lower result as the proportion of women increases (estimate = -0.15, 95% CI: -0.22-0.07, p<0.001). Likewise increasing age seems to significantly lower the result, although this decrease reduces as age bands increase. Sample size has no significant effect. **Framework recommendation: Sex-stratified meta-analysis.** The meta-regression coefficient on proportion-female reaches significance (women_prop p=0.012), warranting separate male and female reference ranges; the meta-regression range remains a useful supplementary view. 
<br>

## pH {.tabset .tabset-pills}
### Framework Recommendation
```{r ph_framework_callout}
framework_callout("ph")
```

### Comment
Although there is substantial heterogeneity across most analyses, the absolute spread of values is relatively tight. There is little absolute difference between sex, age and race with no statistical difference between them. The race sub-analysis suffers from few studies and is likely underpowered. Meta-regression shows stability in the overall result.
	As results seem to be consistent across sensitivity and sub-analyses, we recommend that a single pooled adult range is used.
<br>
